purpose: Four-arm physical event fanout and nonmatching-listener comparison for repaired R100 stack
runtime_commit: R100 event epoch repair plus R99 stack candidate
safety: Guarded private mount/PID/net namespace, before/after stock health and owned-directory cleanup per run
memory: Separate actual registration heap diagnostics; proc RSS/HWM remain diagnostic, not PSS or full peak acceptance.
failure_rule: Stop on collection, correctness, identity, health or cleanup failure; retain raw failed window
analysis: Four exploratory paired randomized blocks, 3 fanout lanes, exact same frozen event client. One operation includes ADD with event receipt, REMOVE with event receipt; byte validation and sequence barriers run in the client. No 1% superiority verdict from four blocks; report every arm and lane.
hypothesis: Check whether lazy borrowed event encoding remains beneficial with one/eight eligible receivers and no eligible receivers after the epoch repair, and whether per-recipient patch/send costs regress.
retention_rule: Reject correctness failures. Report every adverse latency, daemon/client CPU, RSS/HWM and throughput direction. This fanout series does not close lookup/invoke or full-system claims.
build_control: Same actual /tmp/owrt-core-release/ubusd source root, SDK, toolchain, cwd and release flags as before; previous exact-root reconstruction reproduced before bytes.
client_control: ca1a912 client/dependencies plus CPU-clock, register-cycle and register-watch patches; identical client on all four fanout arms. Do not pool other client versions.
metric_directions: Lower is better except ops_per_s, which is higher-is-better. Registration ops are complete add/remove cycles.
